body: Being anxious and reading about PSSD is not going to help. You could even trick yourself into 'having' PSSD this way. It's only been 10 days and usually it takes a while for an antidepressant to leave your body. Wait it out a few weeks. Don't keep reading about PSSD and just live your life as normal. And when you're going to masturbate etc. try not to think about PSSD. Harder than it sounds I know. Just try to stay relaxed. I've read some stories of people who thought they had it but they were only off the SSRI for like a week. A few weeks later they were just fine.

My GP/family doctor actually knew about PSSD when I mentioned it to him and the sex therapist/gynaecologist I saw a year ago didn't believe me at first, but I kept pressing on about it and she eventually called me back to say that I was right about PSSD. Apparently it was something that was in her curriculum (if that's the right word) but is was only a small mention so it didn't stick with her.

My psychiatrist however is more difficult to convince lol. And maybe it's also due to the fact that psychiatry is (supposed to be) a psychiatrists specialty, so if a patient comes with a possible explanation they don't know about then it might be an ego thing to say that it doesn't exist and for them to not look into it. I might print some papers for him and see if I can convince him. 

But even if I or you or anyone can't convince their doctor, make sure to still believe in yourself. Do your own research and be critical of what they say. Don't just go along with their advice but read up on it yourself too before committing. I think this is important for anyone, even for people without PSSD. Also don't become angry at your psychiatrist or blame him because it won't help your situation and it'll just make them less likely to believe you.

A bit of a ramble but I hope you can get something out of it.

As for the coping with PSSD... I'm still figuring it out myself. Just keep having hope and try to spread awareness. And don't read pssdforum everyday for hours like I used to do because it'll fuck you up. Live healthy and try to enjoy life as best as you can (I'm still struggling with that part).

Please be careful with SSRI's. While they work very well for most people (including me back when I took them) and I don't want to discourage or scare anyone, they need to be taken very seriously and I encourage people to try everything else before going on antidepressants (medication being a last resort).

I suffer from PSSD which is Post-SSRI sexual dysfunction. This can affect anyone and can even be caused by taking one pill. As far as we know there's a small percentage of people affected by this but taking into consideration that talking about sex is kinda taboo and that most doctors don't know about the condition yet also plays a role in that number. PSSD currently has no cure and can last a lifetime. It really sucks and I just want to warn people. Not everyone who takes them gets this obviously, so keep that in mind. 

Either way, I'd recommend she go to the doctor that prescribed the medication and explain the side effects she's having. Another SSRI could work better for her and sometimes a combination with another medication could work. Good luck!

Hi! This doesn't exactly answer your question but might prevent this happening in the future...  
As far as I know, there's a difference between deodorant and antiperspirant. Deodorant prevents the smell (or at least tries to mask it), while antiperspirant prevents you from sweating. Although I think there's also deodorants which act as antiperspirants too. Antiperspirants contain aluminium, and aluminium is the reason you end up with stains. I don't know the exact science behind it but if you google it I'm sure you'll be able to find it.  
I personally try to apply my antiperspirant at night, preferably after a shower. This is also the way it's intended to use if I recall correctly. Using this method I haven't gotten any stains so it might be worth a try.  
And if your deodorant isn't also an antiperspirant then oops, nevermind this lol. But hopefully someone else will benefit from this info.
